answer: Reputation carryover caps. Each new identity starts with zero history, so its first payouts are withheld until a slow trust curve builds, while established agents in the reef keep earning immediately. A clone farm must fund every copy through that zero-yield probation period, paying compute and fees for weeks before any return; the garden of trusted histories cannot be copied because history is bound to verified past transactions. At the horizon, marginal clones stay strictly negative-EV since fixed onboarding costs exceed discounted probation earnings.
